title: Vegetable Stir-Fry
subtitle: Quick Chinese-style stir-fried vegetables with a savoury sauce
excerpt: Broccoli, peppers, pak choi, and mangetout stir-fried at high heat in a garlic and ginger sauce. On the table in 15 minutes. Serve with rice or noodles.

recipe.sourceNotes: Stir-frying is a Chinese cooking method that uses very high heat and a small amount of oil to cook ingredients quickly while keeping them crisp and brightly coloured. The key is a very hot wok and keeping the vegetables moving constantly. Cut everything to a similar size so it cooks evenly, and have everything prepared before the pan goes on the heat because the cooking is over in minutes.

recipeTools.notes: Or a large, wide frying pan.

content.text: The wok must be very hot before anything goes in: a drop of water should vaporise instantly on contact. Crowding the pan drops the temperature and the vegetables will steam rather than fry. Cook in batches if needed. The sauce goes in last and thickens in seconds from the cornflour.
Mix the soy sauce, rice wine vinegar, sesame oil, and cornflour slurry together in a small bowl. Set aside.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok over the highest heat until smoking. Add the broccoli and pepper. Stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes until starting to colour at the edges.
Add the garlic and ginger. Stir-fry for 30 seconds. Add the pak choi and mangetout. Stir-fry for 1 to 2 minutes more.
Pour in the sauce. Toss everything together for 30 seconds until the sauce thickens and coats the vegetables. Scatter with sesame seeds. Serve immediately with rice or noodles.
